newsitem.title: JORDAN: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu arrives in Jordan.
newsitem.headline: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu arrives in Jordan.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu arrived in Amman on Sunday for talks with Jordan's King Hussein, witnesses said.
They said Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti met Netanyahu as he alighted from his plane. Netanyahu then set off in a motorcade for his meeting with the king.

Netanyahu, accompanied by his wife Sara, was making his first trip to an Arab state since Israel signed a long-delayed deal with the Palestinians last month on troop withdrawals from the West Bank town of Hebron.

But Jordanian officials, who welcomed the Hebron accord as a positive new beginning for Middle East peace talks, said Sunday's talks would be overshadowed by concerns over Israeli plans to build 6,500 new homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem.

Netanyahu and the king are also expected to discuss encouraging trade between the neighbouring states, who signed a peace treaty in 1994, and proposals for Jordan to give refuge to Moussa Abu Marzook, a leader of the Islamic resistance movement Hamas, held in a New York jail and facing extradition to Israel.
Israeli officials fear a wave of attacks if Abu Marzook is imprisoned in Israel.
